Let $A(-2,0)$ and $B(3,3).$ Find $|\overset{\to }{AB}|.$ Do not round the answer.

$|\overset{\to }{AB}|=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
We have 

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{OA}=a=-2i+0j, \\  & \overset{\to }{OB}=b=3i+3j.\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing $\overset{\to }{AB}$ as the difference of position vectors, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =\overset{\to }{OB}-\overset{\to }{OA} \\  & =b-a \\  & =(3i+3j)-(-2i+0j) \\  & =5i+3j.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{\to }{AB}| & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25+9} \\  & =\sqrt{34}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AC} & =\overset{\to }{OC}-\overset{\to }{OA} \\  & =c-a \\  & =(4i)-(3j) \\  & =4i-3j\end{aligned}

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{\to }{AC}| & =\sqrt{(4)^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+9} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $r=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $s=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $3r+2s$ and points the same direction.
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction., we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{3r+2s}{|3r+2s|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}3r+2s & =3\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+2\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-6)+0 \\ 3+(-6)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|3r+2s| & =\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{45} \\  & =3\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $3r+2s$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{3r+2s}{|3r+2s|} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}(3r+2s) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $r=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -6\end{aligned}].$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $r$ and points the same direction.
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{r}{|\,r\,|}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,r\,| & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+36} \\  & =\sqrt{45} \\  & =3\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $r$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{r}{|r|} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot r \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252505/assets/d1c4fec87897f58b7170a09723fcd2b7f6a2ddcc9ce9a2f52299b7a0580cd922.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252505/assets/ca0a8bd7bfa1ac9750efd56df7960839f64f0414fb086f0c9b24bbd1f3a377ce.svg) Find a unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+2b}{|a+2b|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}a+2b & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2+2 \\ 0+(-2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|a+2b| & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+2b}{|a+2b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(a+2b) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.problem:
Consider the vector $\mathbf{a}=\langle -2,4 \rangle$ shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252505/assets/cd458eeb41ee09d6a4f58bc343575d46e3d362dc3edca40a47e1a7381fcc9bd2.png)

Expressed in component form, our vector is $\mathbf{a}=-2\mathbf{i} + 4 \mathbf{j}.$

To find the magnitude (length) of $\mathbf{a},$ we can use the Pythagorean theorem on $\triangle OXA.$

The legs of the triangle have lengths

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{\to }{OX}| & =|-2|=2\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{\to }{XA}| & =|\,4\,|=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the Pythagorean theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,a\,| & =\sqrt{|\overset{\to }{OX}{|}^{2}+|\overset{\to }{XA}{|}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: General Formula
tutorials.problem:
We just saw that the magnitude of the vector $\mathbf{a}=\langle -2,4 \rangle$ was given by

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,a\,| & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

In general, given a vector
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252505/assets/10fbddb6dc3528629e5583ad25976d049ca2ec5943ce3e689953f79299b8afcd.svg)
the magnitude of the vector can always be computed as

$$

$$

**Note**
